newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Disappearances said still high in north Sri Lanka.
newsitem.headline: Disappearances said still high in north Sri Lanka.

text.p: A Sri Lankan human rights group said on Saturday that some Tamils were disappearing after arrest by security forces in the north despite a marked improvement in the attitude of soldiers towards civilians.

"Cases of disappearance after arrest remain significant," the University Teachers for Human Rights, Jaffna (UTHR) said in a report. "It is clear that routine torture has been sanctioned from the highest levels in the name of security."
The government has failed to publish a list of detainees because some of them had died after torture, the report said.
But the report said there was a marked improvement among many members of the military in their conduct towards civilians in the Jaffna peninsula, 320 km (200 miles) north of Colombo.
"Despite LTTE (Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam) provocation and indiscriminate attacks in public places, there have been no reprisals by the army," it said.

The military spokesman was not immediately available for comment but the Defence Ministry has announced a special inquiry by senior officers into disappearances after complaints from relatives and human rights groups.
A senior military official in Jaffna told Reuters recently that human rights abuses were isolated and committed by rogue soldiers.
The senior Jaffna representative of the International Committee of the Red Cross, Lise Boudreault, recently said there were still abuses, but the situation was improving.
Diplomats and aid workers say the government of President Chandrika Kumaratunga is genuine in trying to stamp out human rights abuses among the security forces.
Nine soldiers and police face trial next year over the rape and murder of a Tamil schoolgirl and the murder of her mother, brother and a neighbour who went looking for her.
If they are found guilty, it would be the first criminal conviction of security personnel for human rights abuses.

The LTTE is fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the mainly Sinhalese Indian Ocean island's north and east. The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year.
